features.definition: 1 if the Pokémon has a bird-like body (beak, feathers, wings as primary limbs), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has an aquatic body form (fish, dolphin, whale, seahorse, octopus, etc.), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon resembles an insect, arachnid, or arthropod, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon resembles a four-legged mammal (dog, cat, bear, etc.), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a clearly humanoid/bipedal body with two arms and two legs, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon visibly has a shell (turtle shell, snail shell, ammonite shell), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has visible wings (feathered, membranous, or insect wings), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has tentacles, fins, or similar appendages, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon incorporates plant elements (leaves, flowers, vines, bark), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon is primarily made of rock, stone, mineral, or metallic material, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon visually suggests ice (icy blue-white coloring, ice crystals, frozen features), 0 otherwise
Degree to which green is the dominant color: 0 = no green, 1 = entirely green
Degree to which blue is the dominant color: 0 = no blue, 1 = entirely blue
Degree to which brown/tan/beige is the dominant color: 0 = none, 1 = entirely brown/tan
Degree to which dark colors (black, dark grey, dark purple) dominate: 0 = none, 1 = entirely dark
Perceived body bulk/size: 0 = very small and compact, 1 = very large and massive
1 if the Pokémon has very large or prominently featured eyes relative to body, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a ghostly, cosmic, or ethereal appearance (floating, translucent, cloud-like, starry), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has visible claws, pincers, or scythes as notable features, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a clearly visible tail, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has visible spikes, horns, or sharp protrusions on its body, 0 otherwise
Degree of roundness/cuteness: 0 = angular/menacing, 1 = very round and cute
1 if the Pokémon stands upright on two legs, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon is visibly covered in fur or feathers, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a hard outer shell or exoskeleton (not counting turtle shells), 0 otherwise
Degree to which orange or red-orange is the dominant color: 0 = no orange/red-orange, 1 = entirely orange/red-orange
Degree to which grey (medium grey, stone grey, not dark black or light white) dominates the color palette: 0 = no grey, 1 = entirely grey
1 if the Pokémon has an overall menacing, aggressive, or threatening appearance (fierce expression, combat stance, dangerous features); 0 if neutral or cute
1 if the Pokémon resembles an ancient sea creature or fossil animal (ammonite, nautilus, trilobite, ancient fish, ancient sea turtle); 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a soft, organic, non-mechanical body without hard armor plating or metallic parts (e.g. whale, jellyfish, slug, plant); 0 if body appears hard, mechanical, or heavily armored
Degree to which green appears as a secondary or accent color even if not dominant: 0 = no green at all, 1 = strong green presence throughout body

1 if the Pokémon has a clearly non-vertebrate or alien body plan (jellyfish, ammonite, trilobite, coral, amoeba, mineral cluster, mechanical orb) that does not resemble any standard vertebrate animal; 0 if it resembles a standard vertebrate (fish, bird, mammal, reptile, humanoid)

Scale from 0 to 1 indicating how much the Pokémon evokes a primordial, ancient, or prehistoric aesthetic through its design elements (fossil-like textures, ancient sea creature forms, primitive organism shapes, archaic patterns). 0 = modern/familiar creature, 1 = strongly ancient/primordial

1 if the Pokémon is primarily based on a plant, mineral/rock/metal object, ghost/spirit, or inanimate object (pot, anchor, bell, etc.) rather than an animal; 0 if it is based on a recognizable animal (vertebrate or invertebrate like insects, crabs, fish, mammals, birds)

1 if the Pokémon clearly resembles a real-world animal (vertebrate like fish, mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, OR invertebrate like insect, crab, jellyfish, squid); 0 if it is based on a plant, mineral, inanimate object, ghost, or purely alien form with no real-world animal analog

Degree to which the Pokémon's overall color palette is cool-toned (blues, teals, purples, grey-blues, icy whites): 0 = no cool colors at all (entirely warm browns/reds/oranges/yellows), 1 = entirely cool-toned (deep blue, teal, icy blue, blue-grey)
Degree to which the Pokémon's dominant color is warm brown, tan, beige, orange, or red-orange: 0 = no warm brown/orange tones, 1 = entirely dominated by warm brown/tan/orange/red-orange colors

Degree to which green color is present in the Pokémon's design, either as primary or secondary color: 0 = absolutely no green anywhere on the Pokémon, 1 = green is very strongly present (dominant or major secondary color throughout)
Degree to which the Pokémon's body (not just accents) is blue or teal colored: 0 = no blue/teal on body, 1 = body is predominantly blue or teal
Degree to which the Pokémon's overall body color falls in the cool teal/cyan/blue-green spectrum: 0 = no teal/cyan/blue-green at all, 1 = body is predominantly teal, cyan, or blue-green colored

Degree to which the Pokémon LACKS warm colors (brown, tan, orange, red, yellow): 0 = heavily dominated by warm brown/tan/orange/red/yellow, 1 = completely free of warm colors (only cool blues, teals, greens, purples, greys)

Degree to which the Pokémon has BOTH warm brown/tan/beige as a body color AND green as a secondary or primary color simultaneously (e.g. a brown animal with green plant elements, a tan creature with green accents). 0 = no combination of brown+green (either no brown, no green, or dominated by other colors like red/blue/pink/dark), 1 = strongly shows brown/tan body with prominent green elements

Degree to which the Pokémon is dominated by warm red, crimson, scarlet, or bright orange-red colors (not brown/tan, not yellow): 0 = no dominant red/orange-red, 1 = strongly dominated by red or orange-red
Degree to which pink, magenta, or light purple is the dominant color of the Pokémon's body: 0 = no pink/magenta/light purple, 1 = body is predominantly pink or magenta

Degree to which the Pokémon has cool blue, teal, or pure green coloring WITHOUT any warm brown/tan/beige body color. Score 1 if the Pokémon is predominantly blue, teal, cyan, or pure green with no brown/tan on its body. Score 0 if the body has warm brown/tan/orange tones OR if the Pokémon has neither cool nor green colors (e.g. pink, red, dark).

Degree to which the Pokémon is dominated by warm red/orange OR pink/magenta colors WITHOUT significant green presence. Score 1 if the Pokémon is primarily red, orange-red, or pink/magenta with little to no green. Score 0 if green is prominent or if the Pokémon is blue/teal/brown.

Degree to which warm brown, tan, beige, or dark brown dominates the Pokémon's body color, regardless of any green accents. Score 1 if the body is predominantly warm brown/tan/dark brown. Score 0 if the body is primarily any other color (blue, green, red, pink, black, grey, yellow).
Score 1 if the Pokémon is primarily dark/black/dark-grey/dark-purple with no dominant warm brown, no dominant blue/teal, and no dominant green or pink. Score 0 otherwise.
Degree to which green is the dominant body color of the Pokémon (not just accents): 0 = no dominant green body color, 1 = body is predominantly green
Degree to which the Pokémon's body is cream, off-white, beige, or very light tan (not pure white, not grey): 0 = no cream/beige coloring, 1 = body is predominantly cream or off-white/beige

Degree to which the Pokémon has a cream, beige, off-white, or light tan body combined with blue or teal accent colors (tentacles, shell markings, fur patches, or body parts). Score 1 if the Pokémon prominently shows both cream/beige body AND blue/teal accents. Score 0 if the body lacks cream/beige OR lacks blue/teal accents entirely.

Degree to which the Pokémon displays BOTH blue or teal coloring AND cream/beige/off-white/light-tan coloring together on its body, regardless of which is dominant. Score 1 if both blue/teal AND cream/beige are clearly present as significant body colors. Score 0 if only one is present or neither is present.

Degree to which the Pokémon has a light-colored warm underbelly, chest, or belly area that is cream, beige, off-white, or pale yellow, contrasting with a darker or more colorful main body. Score 1 if the underbelly/chest is prominently cream/pale/beige. Score 0 if the belly area is the same color as the body or is not light/cream.

Score 1 if the Pokémon has strong, clearly visible green coloring covering a significant portion of its body or design (leaves, green skin, green body parts, green fur/scales). Score 0 if green is absent or only appears as tiny accent dots/small marks. Use only what is visually prominent in the image.

Degree to which the Pokémon's overall color palette is warm-toned (reds, oranges, browns, tans, yellows, warm greens mixed with brown): 0 = entirely cool-toned (blue, teal, icy white, purple, grey with no warm colors), 1 = entirely warm-toned (dominated by red, orange, brown, tan, yellow, or warm green-brown combinations)
Degree to which blue or teal is the dominant palette color of the Pokémon's body, excluding any green or warm tones: 0 = no significant blue/teal presence, 1 = body is overwhelmingly blue or teal

Score 1 if green color (any shade: bright green, dark green, olive green, teal-green) clearly dominates the Pokémon's overall body appearance, covering more than half the visible body surface. Score 0 if the body is primarily any other color (brown, tan, orange, red, blue, grey, black, pink, cream, yellow) even if green appears as a secondary accent.

Degree to which the Pokémon's body color is muted, neutral, or desaturated (grey, beige, tan, dull brown, dark grey, stone, sandy) WITHOUT being dominated by vivid colors (not bright red, orange, yellow, pink, blue, teal, green). Score 1 if the Pokémon is overwhelmingly muted/neutral grey-brown-tan-dark. Score 0 if the body is dominated by any vivid color (green, blue, teal, red, orange, pink, yellow).

Degree to which the Pokémon is dominated by VIVID warm colors that are NOT muted brown/tan - specifically bright red, scarlet, crimson, vivid orange, bright yellow, or hot pink/magenta. Score 1 if vivid red/orange/yellow/pink strongly dominates the body. Score 0 if the body is muted/neutral, or green, or blue/teal.

Degree to which the Pokémon's body is dominated by vivid cool colors - specifically bright blue, teal, cyan, or blue-purple - WITHOUT significant green. Score 1 if vivid blue/teal/cyan dominates the body with little green. Score 0 if body is green, brown, red/orange, pink, or muted/neutral.

notes: The grouping criterion appears to be color palette category: 1) GREEN dominant Pokémon, 2) NEUTRAL/MUTED Pokémon (grey, brown, tan, dark without vivid color), 3) WARM VIVID Pokémon (red, orange, yellow, pink dominant), 4) COOL VIVID Pokémon (blue, teal dominant). item_029 (sandy tan) groups with grey/dark/muted brown Pokémon, away from vivid red/orange, away from blue/cream fossils. The key distinction within non-green is muted/neutral vs vivid warm vs vivid cool.
